subject: Renewal negotiation: commit + capacity uplift options
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@novatech.io>

Cc: procurement@novatech.io
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal negotiation: scale and pricing

Hi Irene,

Our renewal for Novatech (current term expires 2028-07-31) is coming up and we need to lock pricing and capacity for the next 12–24 months. Usage has grown faster than forecasted — Q1+Q2 consumption attached — and we expect a meaningful uplift across embeddings and chat generation.

Key asks from procurement:
- A 12-month price hold (no per-token increases) while we complete procurement.
- A competitive discount off list for a renewed commit; target ~20% if possible.
- Some form of one-time credits to smooth the transition for the first billing quarter.

We’re open to a multi-year commit if the economics are right; also would consider a staged uplift where we agree to a baseline commit and add a capacity add-on at a fixed rate.

Can you share concrete options (short bridge vs. multi-year commit) and a ballpark redline for legal/procurement? We’d like to present something to our CFO and procurement team by next Wednesday (2028-06-17).

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales

Hi Elena — thanks for the usage summary, that helps. I pulled together three options below so you can see trade-offs quickly; attaching a short brief and a draft order form.

Option A — 3-month bridge (short-term)
- 10% discount off current published tiered rates for three months
- $50k one-time credit applied to first invoice
- No long-term commit; standard pay-as-you-go thereafter
- Good if procurement needs immediate price stability while evaluating longer-term terms

Option B — 12-month firm commit + 12-month price hold (recommended)
- 18% average discount across chat/embeddings with tiered step-down at higher usage bands
- Guaranteed price hold for 12 months from effective date
- $75k onboarding/transition credit to offset Q3 spike
- Option to purchase a capacity uplift add-on at fixed per-unit rates (pre-agreed)

Option C — 24-month committed plan with capacity uplift
- 20% baseline discount for a 24-month commit with annual true-up
- $100k annual uplift commitment required (min spend increase) to qualify for the 20% rate
- 12-month price hold, then standard annual CPI-based adjustments capped at X% (we can specify)

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick alignment call (30m) to pick a preferred option, 2) we draft an order form/term sheet and send to your procurement and legal. I can also surface this to our sales leadership if you need a higher discount band or credits.

Links: renewal-options-brief.pdf (attached) | order form (draft attached)

Would you be available tomorrow 11:30–12:00 PT or Wednesday 08:30–09:00 PT?

Best,

Irene and David,

I’m supportive of Option B as the default customer-facing proposal. We can push to 20% but discounts north of 15% require Legal + Revenue Ops sign-off and a contracting rationale (multi-year, minimum ARR uplift, or strategic reference). Recommend we present: 18% across the board, $75k transition credit, 12-month price hold, and the capacity add-on at fixed unit pricing.

Elena — quick note from Solutions/Presales on capacity and commitment impact.

We ran the usage profile you sent through a sizing model; a 24-month commit materially reduces per-token latency/cost because it lets us presize Dedicated pools and plan batching. Practically, that means we can make a stronger discount offer for a longer firm commitment. A few operational considerations:
- If Novatech needs predictable throughput at peak, we recommend the capacity uplift be defined as a committed burst pool allocation (not just soft burst), with explicit SLOs.
- The $75–100k credits are fine as onboarding/true-up offsets; we should keep the credit as invoice credit rather than decreasing committed ARR so it doesn’t impact reporting.
- For legal: we can include a 12-month explicit price hold in the order form and an annual CPI cap thereafter.

Concrete counterproposal (to enable procurement signoff):
- 24-month firm commit: baseline spend $1.6M/year (commit level)
- 20% discount off list across committed units for 24 months (subject to baseline uplift of min $100k in year 1)
- $100k onboarding credit applied in Q1 invoice after effective date
- Price hold guaranteed for months 1–12; CPI cap of 3% for year 2

If that aligns with procurement we can prepare a signed order form and DocuSign bundle by end of week. Happy to jump on the call to walk procurement through the SLOs and uplift mechanics.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwoodinference.com
